newsitem.title: FINLAND: SUOMI SUPERVISORS OKAY POHJOLA RESHUFFLE.
newsitem.headline: SUOMI SUPERVISORS OKAY POHJOLA RESHUFFLE.

text.p: Mutual insurer Suomi said in a statement on Tuesday its supervisory board had approved insurer Pohjola's plan to take over its life-insurer Salama and set the price at 537 million markka.

"The supervisory board of Suomi decided that Suomi will sell its holding in Salama, 92 percent of share capital, to Pohjola at a price of 537.3 million markka, and that the company will give up underwriting new business against a compensation totalling 54 million markka," Suomi said in a statement.
The final price would be adjusted at completion to reflect changes in net asset value from January 1 to June 30, it said.

"The price for Salama represents a premium to net adjusted value after a strengthening of Salama's reserve by allocating 20 percent of unrealised capital gains to Salama policyholders," Suomi said in the statement.

The price of the shares and the payment to Suomi for refraining from underwriting new business were based on a valuation of Salama's shares and Suomi's new business drawn up by the British investment bank Fox-Pitt, Kelton, Suomi said.
